perspective:
Christian’s accessible information:

- He and Jonathan have been close friends since childhood; Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice and values his perspective.
- Christian recently felt Jonathan was acting differently and became anxious/suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important.
- Christian arranged and attended a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- He heard Jonathan admit that something was being hidden: Jonathan said he was in trouble and hadn’t known how to tell Christian.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic, offered help, and said they could face it together.
- He heard Jonathan say the situation was complicated, that he didn’t want to drag Christian in, but then Jonathan accepted support/resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian began to believe the trouble might involve criminal/illegal activity. He asked Jonathan directly.
- He heard Jonathan say he couldn’t be sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he hadn’t done anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into it discreetly; Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up. He told Jonathan this and said he had leads and would gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian later believed/found out that the real culprit was someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He felt betrayed and resolved to confront that person and bring them to justice. He told Jonathan this; Jonathan warned him the person was dangerous but trusted Christian to do what is right.
- The specific identity of that culprit is not stated in the provided dialogue, though Christian believes he has identified someone close to them.
